question.text: Aravali Long-Short Fund (Cat III AIF, determinate trust) earns FY25: F&O net gain INR 18 crore, LTCG on listed equity (STT-paid) INR 4 crore, STCG on listed equity (STT-paid) INR 3 crore, dividend INR 2 crore. Assuming the fund discharges tax at fund level as representative assessee (practical approach) and NO Section 161(1A) tainting is invoked, at which rate is the F&O gain taxed?

answer.text: MMR of 42.744% as 'Profits and gains from business or profession'

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook Para 16.2.5: gains from F&O transactions in a Cat III AIF are treated as 'Profits and gains from business or profession' and taxed at MMR (42.744% — 30% basic + 37% surcharge + 4% cess). LTCG/STCG/dividend sleeves are taxed at their respective head-wise effective rates at the fund level. Here 18 cr x 42.744% = INR 7,69,39,200 fund-level tax on the F&O sleeve alone. The Trap: Option A applies LTCG concessional rate to business income — incorrect. Option B ignores the surcharge and cess layer. Option C confuses Cat III with Cat I/II. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B covers fund-level rates from a client-return angle; XIX-C expects fund-level computation and quarterly advance tax discipline. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep a PAN-level tax calendar. Pay advance tax in four instalments — 15/45/75/100% — to avoid 234B/234C interest. Cat III fund-level tax on F&O at MMR means large quarterly cash outflows; plan treasury accordingly.
